clean_areas: Coverage-by-construction: planEdgarFetch (Tier 2) and planEdgarFetchIncremental (Tier 1) both derive their month set from the same EDGAR_FLOOR_START constant and the same pure enumerateMonths(floorStart, asOf) (extract/edgar-fetch-plan.ts:58,110-113,132-146; extract/edgar.ts:31-43). Tier 1 plans EVERY month missing from the persisted floor (not just the trailing revision window) plus the 2-month revision window, so no month is ever permanently unreachable by either tier; Tier 2 unconditionally re-plans the full range regardless of persisted state. Verified against source, not assumed.

Tier-selection determinism/replay-safety: selectEdgarRefreshTier(asOf) (edgar-incremental-refresh.ts:80-86) reads only its asOf string argument via `new Date(`${asOf}T00:00:00Z`).getUTCDay()` — no Date.now()/wall-clock call anywhere in the function. Confirmed by direct read of the implementation (not inferred from comments) and independently asserted by backend/tests/edgar-incremental-refresh.test.ts:49 ('is a pure function of asOf alone — same input, same output, no hidden clock dependency'), which passed on a live run.

No tier-decision drift between call sites: analytics/index.ts:294 computes `edgarTier = selectEdgarRefreshTier(asof)` to size `deadlineAt`, and access/data-source.ts:113,137,141-146 passes that same `asof` string unchanged into `refreshEdgarIncremental({ asOf: asof, ... })`, which internally recomputes `tier = opts.tier ?? selectEdgarRefreshTier(opts.asOf)` (edgar-incremental-refresh.ts:167) on the identical input. Since both computations are the same pure function applied to the same string, the deadline-sizing tier and the tier actually executed can never disagree — traced end to end, not asserted from comments alone.

No duplicate/double-counted rows across a tier switch: the durable write path (raw-history-store.ts:48-71) does `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (date, indicator) DO UPDATE SET value = EXCLUDED.value, source = EXCLUDED.source` — a true upsert keyed on (date, indicator), not an append. The in-memory merge used to build the signal-computation bundle (transform/math.ts:356-376, `mergeSeries`) is also a Map keyed by date with fetched values overwriting prior values. A Tier-1-then-Tier-2 (or reverse) sequence re-submitting an already-persisted month is therefore idempotent by construction on both the DB floor and the in-memory series.

Whole-batch-degrade honesty model applies identically to both tiers: refreshEdgarIncremental (edgar-incremental-refresh.ts:160-283) and validateEdgarBatch (extract/edgar-fetch-plan.ts:178-235) are single shared code paths for both tiers — only the `plan` array's origin differs (planEdgarFetch vs planEdgarFetchIncremental at edgar-incremental-refresh.ts:169-177). Deadline-abort and per-month validation failure both discard the ENTIRE batch (`newRows: []`) regardless of which tier produced the plan; Tier 1's smaller plan size changes only how fast a failure surfaces, not the discard-on-any-failure semantics.

Tests execute for real, not silently skipped: `bun test tests/edgar-incremental-refresh.test.ts tests/edgar-fetch-plan.test.ts` (36 pass/0 fail) and `bun test tests/research-last-good.test.ts tests/research-fidelity.test.ts tests/api/analytics-edgar.test.ts` (6 pass/0 fail) both ran live against an ephemeral Postgres instance with real migrations, exercising tier purity, month-boundary planning, idempotent replay for both tiers, the failure matrix, and end-to-end index.ts wiring including a concretely-located real Sunday for tier 'full' (tests/api/analytics-edgar.test.ts:62). No mocked-away subject, no `.skip`.
